dependencies.name: analysis-target
dependencies.summary: a real project for the CLI to analyze — the subject every analysis flow reaches its verdict against

registration.description: path to a checked-out project on this machine; it is COPIED into the sandbox, so the run never touches the original

needs.need: a project the deterministic scan finds at least one violation in EVERY category the analyze report names — Code quality, Security, Bugs, Architecture, Performance, Reliability, Database and Style — and whose sources include TypeScript (.ts), JavaScript (.js) and Python (.py) files

more than 20 deterministic findings, so the default listing is a partial twenty-wide window with a next-page pointer and `--all` is visibly a different shape, plus at least one critical-or-high finding and at least one below it so the severity filter has something to leave out
more than 20 deterministic findings, so the default listing paginates and `--all` can be told apart from it, plus at least one critical-or-high finding alongside at least one of a lower severity
at least one deterministic finding, so a severity-filtered listing renders its violation count instead of the empty state
at least one source file the LLM rules accept, so the run reports a non-zero file count, and at least one deterministic finding so the baseline run's violation summary is not empty
at least one source file the LLM rules accept, so the run reports a non-zero file count, and at least one deterministic finding so the violation summary is not empty

dependencies.name: claude-login
dependencies.summary: an authenticated Claude Code installation — a long-lived token from `claude setup-token`, the state `claude -p` needs before it will answer

condition.sentence: only when the LLM transport is `claude-code`; the `api` transport reaches the model with a key instead

vars.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
vars.description: a long-lived token from `claude setup-token`; it is exported into the sandbox child, so the spawned `claude` authenticates with it and your real login state is never read or touched

needs.need: a long-lived token from `claude setup-token` that answers a non-interactive `claude -p` prompt without prompting for authentication

dependencies.name: llm-api-credentials
dependencies.summary: a provider API account the CLI can reach the model through directly

condition.sentence: only when the LLM transport is `api`; the `claude-code` transport uses a local login instead

vars.name: provider
vars.description: the provider id `truecourse config llm setup --provider` is given (anthropic | openai | bedrock | copilot)

vars.name: model
vars.description: a model id that provider serves, as `--model` takes it

vars.name: api-key
vars.description: an API key for that provider with enough quota to complete one analysis

vars.name: base-url
vars.description: the provider API base URL — omit for the provider default

needs.need: a key whose live provider probe succeeds, because `config llm setup` verifies the account before it saves anything

dependencies.name: dotnet-sdk
dependencies.summary: the built C# Roslyn semantic host — without it, analyzing C# fails hard by design (there is no tree-sitter-only fallback)

condition.sentence: only when the analyzed project contains C#

vars.name: TRUECOURSE_ROSLYN_HOST
vars.description: absolute path to the built host (`dotnet build -c Release tools/csharp-roslyn-host`), which needs the .NET 8 SDK once per checkout
